title: ResourceQueueService
responsibility: Validates and owns queued or running leases, enforces inherited reservations and releases them after any outcome.

inputs.name: ResourceQueueService.constructor.options
inputs.description: The constructor reads env from options.env or process.env, resolves home from options.home or resourceHome(env), and passes options.monitor to ResourceMonitorService. These options configure the service's environment, home path, and monitor adapter.

inputs.name: ResourceQueueService.run.input
inputs.description: The request is parsed with resourceRequestSchema before it is enqueued. For inherited leases, its cpus and memoryMiB values must not exceed the running parent reservation.

inputs.name: ResourceQueueService.run.action
inputs.description: The callback runs after monitor.wait completes and the post-wait abort check passes. It receives a ResourceContext, and its resolved value is returned by run.

inputs.name: ResourceQueueService.run.options
inputs.description: The options are passed to monitor.wait, with env overriding the service environment and signal checked before enqueue and after waiting. If supplied, waitTimeoutMs must be finite and greater than zero.

outputs.name: ResourceQueueService.snapshot
outputs.description: Each call resolves with the value returned by the owned ResourceMonitorService.snapshot() method. This service does not transform or cache that value.

outputs.name: ResourceQueueService.run
outputs.description: Resolves with the value returned by action after the queue wait and post-wait abort check succeed. Once enqueued, the request is removed in finally after either waiting or action execution.

outputs.name: ResourceQueueService.close
outputs.description: Calls close() on the service's owned ResourceQueueRepository.

errors.name: Resource request validation, capacity, or admission failure
errors.description: This Error is thrown for an invalid wait timeout, an owner without startedAt, a full queue of 512 records, an invalid inherited lease, or nested CPU or memory above the parent reservation. Request parsing, abort checks, monitor waits, action execution, snapshot reads, and queue closing can also propagate their underlying failures.
